decisions.reason: The battery-efficiency goal does not change the established single-board consolidation or functionality-preservation attributes.
Battery efficiency is a separate power-management objective and does not modify the current cost, component-tier, connector-reduction, or functionality-preservation constraints.
The general battery-efficiency objective does not necessarily change the existing source OR-ing method, sources, or source-selection behavior.
The source does not change the DCDC1 voltage setpoint, configuration interface, downstream target, or diode-drop compensation.
The battery-efficiency goal does not entail any change to the connector inventory or connector architecture.
The source does not alter the required LED-board power and data pin ordering.
Maximizing battery operating time does not necessarily change the monitor IC, monitored rails, channel count, or measurement placement.
The efficiency objective does not specify a change to the battery connector, pinout, voltage range, placement, or AXP2101 connection.
The source adds an operating-time objective but does not modify any battery-protection mode or cutoff requirement.
The battery-efficiency goal does not change the required NTC-based temperature-sensing method.
The source does not change how charge status is indicated or any associated connector and resistor configuration.
The battery-efficiency objective does not entail a change to the power board's dimensions, orientation, placement, mounting, or connector-access layout.
